_README: FROZEN acceptance-coverage debt ceiling — enforced by
Semantics: ceilings.status.<status> and ceilings.debt_class.<A|B|C|D> are the
MAXIMUM number of criteria that may carry that status / class. Measured >
ceiling => CI FAILS. ceilings.total_criteria is a FLOOR, not a ceiling: the
corpus may grow, never shrink, so deleting an inconvenient `partial` row
cannot read as progress. Measured < ceiling => CI prints the tightened block
for you to paste back here; lowering a ceiling after real work is expected.
Every number here is MEASURED DEBT, not an allowance. There is no headroom by
design: a ceiling set above the measured figure would silently license the
next unproven criterion. Raising one is an adjudication recorded in
This ratchet bounds how much of the acceptance contract is UNPROVEN. It is not
a project-completion figure: a criterion counted here may well be implemented
correctly — the claim is only that nothing in the suite asserts it.

provenance.slice: acceptance batch 18 (doc 10 - Rationale Families, BACKEND surface). Two criteria closed: RF-07 and RF-12, in both cases the criterion's LAST open clause, so both lose their debt_class. No product code changed; the diff is two integration cases plus one optional harness parameter. RF-07.c2: the pre-existing test_duplicate_active_name_conflicts asserts the raise and stops, which cannot distinguish a guard placed ABOVE rationale_repo.create_family from one placed BELOW it - both raise the identical exception. The new test counts RationaleFamilyRoot / RationaleFamilyRevision rows around the refusal and re-reads the surviving revision (original casing intact, revision_no still 1). It deliberately does NOT roll back after the raise: a rollback would discard a duplicate row and let a post-insert guard pass vacuously, so it uses flush() + expire_all() and reads back inside the same transaction. RF-12.c3: the validator half was proven at unit level (a missing and a blank rationale_family_id both yield STRATEGY_CONFIG_INVALID / NOT_READY), but no test drove a family-less composition through request_backtest_run, so the 'NOT_READY -> READINESS_BLOCKED, nothing persisted' half rode on a code path proven only for OTHER blockers (shared allocation, empty composition). The new test builds the SAME composition that admits happily in test_admission_queues_run_and_worker_materializes_result and differs ONLY in the omitted Family. _strategy_payload gained rationale_family_id: str | None = 'rf_1', where None OMITS the key rather than storing a null - create_work_object persists the payload verbatim and performs no StrategyConfig validation, so the omission survives to Ready Check exactly as a real family-less Strategy would, and every existing caller is byte-identical. THREE negative controls, each read for WHICH assertion went red. (1) Moving _check_name_available from the top of _op to below rationale_repo.create_family raises the SAME exception, leaves test_duplicate_active_name_conflicts GREEN, and reddens only the new test on the root count (assert 2 == 1) - which is precisely why RF-07.c2 was open. (2) Giving rationale_family_id a default so a family-less config parses turns the composition 'ready' and reddens the readiness assertion; this control exists SPECIFICALLY because the branch changed a shared harness - without it the refusal could have been attributed to some other blocker the new parameter broke. (3) Writing a BacktestRun row before the readiness gate throws the same exception but reddens the run-count assertion. Product code was restored byte-for-byte after each control. ONE NEW FINDING, RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON: RF-08.c2 - see the adjudication entry RF_08_c2_reserved_name_ships_no_remediation. Doc 10's remaining open rows are RF-08 (that finding) and RF-18 (a frontend clause), so doc 10's BACKEND acceptance debt is now zero. NUMBERING: authored as ADIM 93 / batch 17, then twice renumbered as competing PRs merged first - #804 took ADIM 93, and #808 took BOTH ADIM 94 and batch 17 (doc 01 Mainboard). This record is therefore ADIM 95 / batch 18. Each number was measured from what main actually carries, not from PR titles.
provenance.conditions: static scan for the ledger figures; both new cases and all three negative controls WERE executed against a real PostgreSQL 16 provisioned in this session container and migrated with `alembic upgrade head`, on an ISOLATED TEST_DATABASE_URL (test_rationale_persistence.py 17 -> 18 passed; test_backtest_persistence.py green end to end, which also proves the optional harness parameter left its ~30 existing callers unchanged; #804's test_strategy_integration.py and #805's test_oracle_portfolio_containment_gate.py were run alongside and are green). Backend lint / format / type gates run locally and clean. The frontend was untouched. The FULL backend suite and its coverage gate are left to CI, which reported `Backend - lint, type, test` green on the immediately preceding head (37e5f45); no local pass count or coverage figure is asserted for this branch.
provenance.supersedes: the batch 17 freeze (73 partial / 7 uncovered; A1 B41 C6 D32, base fb3d771 via #808, doc 01 Mainboard MB-01 + MB-27). THE CHAINING NOTE FIRED FOUR TIMES ON THIS ONE BRANCH. It was frozen in turn against 3994725 (77/45), d47c5ba after #804 (73/41), and finally fb3d771 after #808 (71/39); #807, #805 and #802 also landed in between but touch no audit file, so the ceiling held across those. Every figure was measured with --ratchet on the tree it names; none was derived by subtracting two freezes. NOTE the coincidence that would mislead hand arithmetic: this branch and #808 BOTH close exactly two criteria, so both independently produce a 2-point drop, and the pre-#808 freeze of this branch carried the same 73/41 numbers #808 later wrote for entirely different criteria. The batches are disjoint (RF-07/RF-12 on doc 10 versus MB-01/MB-27 on doc 01) and touch disjoint test files, which is why both closures survive.

adjudication.why_a_ceiling_and_not_a_failure: Turning 139 open criteria into a hard CI failure blocks every unrelated PR behind work no single slice can do. Leaving them unbounded is how the number grew unnoticed. The ceiling is the same trade frontend/e2e/a11y-baseline.json already makes: today's debt is frozen, and only GROWTH is red.
adjudication.class_D_is_not_test_debt: 32 of the open criteria name an error code, model field, validator or Agent Tool Gateway member that does not exist in backend/src. No test can close them; counting them as coverage debt budgets product work to a test slice. They are ratcheted separately so that closing class B cannot mask class D growing.
adjudication.class_C_is_never_closable: 6 criteria rest on a clause that is not assertable by nature — a statement about the V18 mockup document, another page's document scope, a V1 feature deliberately left closed (retention auto-purge, doc 20 §16), or a scenario Production cannot construct (CP-06, SUPPORTED_TARGET_RUNTIMES == {python}). Their ceiling must never be driven to zero; driving it down would mean someone invented a product to satisfy a document sentence.
adjudication.O-31_active_run_refusal_name: Three page documents named ONE refusal three ways: ACTIVE_RUN_DEPENDENCY (doc 03 §14, doc 04 §15), DELETE_BLOCKED_BY_RUNNING_JOB (doc 20 §15) and OBJECT_IN_ACTIVE_RUN (doc 01/15). Only the last ships. Settled the O-02 way — the SHIPPED name is canonical, the other two are historical — and pinned by backend/tests/integration/test_backtest_persistence.py::test_active_run_blocks_work_object_delete, which now asserts the wire code and http_status 409 instead of the exception class alone.
adjudication.class_B_batches_are_deliberately_small: 101 open class-B criteria cannot be closed in one pass without the review degenerating into a rubber stamp — and a criterion marked covered by a test that does not actually prove it is worse than one honestly left partial. Batches are therefore scoped to one page document and one surface (batch 01 = doc 05, backend). Each closed clause cites a node that fails when the behaviour is removed; where the assertion could plausibly pass vacuously it was negative-controlled by hand (see the notes on TL-03, TL-15 and TL-17 in acceptance_semantic_map.yaml).
adjudication.TL_11_c3_is_very_likely_class_C_not_B: ADIM 49 finding, recorded rather than acted on. TL-11.c3 names a run over an ALLOCATION-ENABLED composition. Shared capital allocation is fail-closed at ADMISSION in this build (domain/allocation/capability.py SHARED_ALLOCATION_STATUS = 'future_dev'; commands/backtest_run.py raises ALLOCATION_SHARED_MODE_NOT_IN_BUILD before any run, manifest or job exists), so the run the clause describes cannot be constructed and NO test can close it. That is the class C definition, not class B. It was NOT moved: B -> C would RAISE the C ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication. ADIM 48's kickoff recommended this row as closable; that was wrong. Two such findings are now open — this and TL-16 (c4 wants a 409 field that does not exist, so class D).
adjudication.three_more_doc12_clauses_look_misclassif: ADIM 54 findings, recorded rather than acted on — the same shape as the TL-11.c3 finding of ADIM 52. RD-01.c4 wants an ANALYSIS-time DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED gate that does not exist and is not needed (market_entity_id is required at create). RD-05.c5 wants an Agent research draft/analysis tool; ToolName exposes none. RD-11.c2 wants the evidence bundle to pin feature definitions, time policies and mapping ids; _seal_bundle members carry five fields and none of those three. None was moved: B -> C/D RAISES a ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication. FIVE such findings are now open across the ledger (TL-11.c3, TL-16, TL-01.c4 and these three clauses), which is itself the signal: ADIM 42 classified from each record's own notes without re-reading product code, and said so.
adjudication.PC_02_c2_empty_input_text_is_unconstruct: ADIM 75 finding, recorded rather than acted on — the ninth of this shape, and the second on doc 07. PC-02.c2 wants the Pre-Check surface to show a 'final empty-input text' for an EMPTY SOURCE (doc 07 §16: 'UI shows TA PRE-CHECK RESULT with final empty-input text'). Measured on base 0f0651d, two independent reasons it is not class B. (1) The copy does not exist: EMPTY_SOURCE appears NOWHERE in frontend/src, and the only EmptyState on the Pre-Check page (pages/PreCheck.tsx:123) reads 'No requests yet' — an empty request LIST, not an empty source. (2) Decisively, the state is UNCONSTRUCTIBLE on the shipped surface: the overlay renders as `{precheckOpen && detail !== null ? <PreCheckModal … />}` (pages/CreatePackage.tsx:765), so Pre-Check cannot be opened without a persisted request, while a request with an empty source can never be persisted because normalize_request raises EMPTY_SOURCE at the route before the DB. There is no reachable screen on which an empty-input Pre-Check result could render, which is the class C definition ('a scenario Production cannot construct'), not test debt. It was NOT moved: B -> C would RAISE the C ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication. Note this differs from PC-20.c3 on the same document: that one IS constructible and simply unimplemented (class D), whereas this one cannot be reached at all.
adjudication.PC_20_c3_restored_request_staleness_is_c: ADIM 72 finding, recorded rather than acted on — the eighth of this shape. PC-20.c3 says 'a restored package REQUEST comes back stale'. Doc 07 §5's 'deleted / restored request' lifecycle row does demand it ('restored request current dependencies için stale kabul edilir'), but NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT. Measured on base df7df92: a package request IS a trashable registry root (entity_type='package_request'), so the scenario is constructible and this is not class C. Restore, however, goes through commands/deletion.py::_restore_registry_target — the generic branch — which only returns deletion_state to ACTIVE and clears deleted_at/deleted_by/delete_reason. There is no package-request branch (the typed ones are backtest_result, manual_document, hypothesis_artifact). cp_repo.get_current_scan then reads detail.current_scan_id through a plain session.get with NO deletion filter, so the pre-delete PASSED scan survives intact, and _enforce_precheck_gate compares only context_hash and registry_fingerprint — neither of which a delete/restore cycle moves. A restored request therefore passes the Send gate instead of coming back stale. Closing this needs a restore-time staleness marker (product work), so the row is class D, not test debt. It was NOT moved: B -> D would RAISE the D ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication.
adjudication.doc16_event_names_are_shipped_names: ADIM 55. Doc 16 names two audit events RESULT_SOFT_DELETED and RESULT_RESTORED. Neither string exists: the shipped kinds are `backtest.result_soft_deleted` (written by the command) and `trash.restored` (written by the generic trash restore path). Settled the O-02 / O-31 way — the SHIPPED name is canonical and the document's is historical — and the restore assertion additionally pins target_entity_id to the result id, so it proves THIS result's restore was audited rather than that some trash activity occurred. Renaming shipped event kinds to match a document sentence would break every consumer for a spelling.
adjudication.AL_06_c3_is_frontend_not_backend_debt: ADIM 83 note, not a reclassification. AL-06 keeps debt_class B with one open clause: c3 ('the textarea content is preserved for the user after the rejection') is a frontend behaviour and batch 11 was scoped to doc 18's BACKEND surface, the same one-document-one-surface rule every batch since batch 01 has followed. The clause is closable — analysisLab.test.tsx simply has no directive-validation case yet — so it is ordinary class-B test debt awaiting a doc 18 FRONTEND batch, not a finding. Doc 18's backend-testable debt is now zero. CLOSED by acceptance batch 13 (this freeze), which took doc 18's FRONTEND surface and added the missing directive-validation case. The note is kept rather than deleted so the record shows the clause was carried deliberately for exactly one batch, not overlooked.
adjudication.TL_16_c4_409_carries_no_canonical_state: ADIM 84 finding, recorded rather than acted on -- the tenth of this shape, and the third on doc 05. TL-16.c4 says 'the 409 envelope carries the server's canonical current state'. MEASURED on base 7f331c7: every raise site of WorkObjectRevisionConflictError is bare -- 'raise WorkObjectRevisionConflictError()' in commands/trade_log.py, commands/trading_signal.py and commands/mainboard.py, with no argument at any of the three. shared/errors.py::AppError.__init__ then sets self.details = details or [] and leaves scope_id / field_path / remediation at their class defaults, and WorkObjectRevisionConflictError declares none of them. So the published 409 carries code, message, category, retryable and suggested_action -- and nothing whatsoever about the root's current head revision id. There is no field for a test to read, which is the class D definition (the code the criterion names does not exist), not test debt. Note this differs from TL-11.c3 on the same document: that clause is unconstructible (class C shape), whereas this one is perfectly constructible and simply unimplemented. It was NOT moved: B -> D would RAISE the D ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication. TL-16 therefore stays partial / class B even though c3 closed in this slice. Fixing it would widen the O-02 error envelope, so it is a product decision rather than a test slice's call.
adjudication.TL_22_c4_is_defended_by_two_gates_not_on: ADIM 84 measurement, recorded because it changes how the row must be negative-controlled. 'The human Mainboard is not auto-mutated by the Agent's work' is enforced twice over: commands/trade_log.py::_resolve_attach_workspace resolves the default board THROUGH THE ACTOR (queries/mainboard.py::get_default_mainboard filters on actor.principal_id), and commands/mainboard.py::_require_owned_workspace independently refuses a workspace the actor does not own. Breaking only the first therefore turns the test red at 'status == succeeded' with a REJECTED tool call -- red for the wrong reason, proving the ownership gate rather than the assertion under test. The controls that count disabled BOTH gates (the workspace-identity assertion went red) and leaked a row_version bump onto a bystander board inside mainboard.py::_recompute_composition_hash (the board-state assertion went red). A future batch re-measuring this row should not read the first control's red as evidence.
adjudication.TL_18_was_a_bookkeeping_miss_not_missing: ADIM 88 measurement. TL-18 sat at uncovered/class B with the note 'Nothing in the suite asserts this', but frontend/src/test/presentationState.test.tsx had asserted exactly it since ADIM 60 (d012a63, PR #719) -- its describe block names TL-18 by id, and its two sibling criteria TS-16 and AOS-16 cite those very nodes as covered. The note was simply never revisited after the test landed. Recorded because the failure mode is systemic, not local: a criterion can be proven by a node whose own describe block names it and still read as debt for five waves. Before planning any batch, grep the test tree for the criterion id -- it is cheaper than writing a test that already exists. Falsifiability was measured rather than assumed: adding a PATCH to the three onClick handlers in pages/Mainboard.tsx turns both nodes red, so this is a one-point break, not the three-point (unfalsifiable) shape recorded for TL-02.c2. A first attempt at that control modified NOTHING because the handler string occurs three times and the patch asserted a single occurrence; the run stayed green and would have been a false negative control had the assertion not caught it.
adjudication.MB_22_c4_restore_returns_the_report_to_C: ADIM 94 finding, recorded rather than acted on -- the eleventh of this shape, and the second about a restore path (compare PC-20.c3). MB-22.c4 says 'after a restore the previous Ready report is no longer usable and must be rerun'. MEASURED on base d47c5ba with a throwaway probe driven against a real database, then deleted: the SHIPPED behaviour is the OPPOSITE. repositories/mainboard.py::list_active_items joins EntityRegistry and filters deletion_state == ACTIVE, so a soft delete drops the item out of the composition and the fingerprint moves -- the report correctly reads STALE at that point. A RESTORE puts the very same (root_id, revision_id) back, so queries/readiness_check.py::_current_fingerprint recomputes the ORIGINAL value byte-for-byte and is_stale() returns False: the pre-delete report reads 'ready' / is_current True again. The probe printed the three fingerprints in order -- 02edaff5.. then 9e72b8a1.. then 02edaff5.. -- so this is measured, not argued. Nothing marks a restored composition as needing a rerun; closing the clause needs a restore-time staleness marker, which is product work. That is the class D definition (the mechanism the criterion names does not exist), not test debt, and the scenario is perfectly constructible so it is not class C. It was NOT moved: B -> D would RAISE the D ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication. MB-22 therefore stays partial / class B even though its siblings are proven.
adjudication.RF_08_c2_reserved_name_ships_no_remediat: ADIM 95 finding, recorded rather than acted on - the eleventh of this shape, and the first on doc 10. RF-08.c2 says the RATIONALE_FAMILY_NAME_RESERVED error 'surfaces restore / rename / different-name recovery options to the caller'. Doc 10 §10.1's error table supplies the exact string ('Restore/rename old Family where appropriate, or choose a different name') and §8.2 item 4 repeats it. MEASURED: shared/errors.py::RationaleFamilyNameReserved declares only `code` and `message`, and its single raise site (commands/rationale.py::_check_name_available) is a bare `raise RationaleFamilyNameReserved()`. AppError.__init__ therefore leaves remediation and suggested_action at their None class defaults, so the published 409 carries no recovery text at all; the `message` names ONE of the three options ('Choose a different name') and is silent on restore and rename. IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM TL-16.c4, the closest sibling: that clause needs the O-02 envelope WIDENED, whereas this one needs nothing new - `remediation` is already part of the shipped envelope and TWENTY error classes in the same file declare one (e.g. StaleRevisionError, the timezone errors). So this is a one-line class-level `remediation = ...` with copy the spec already dictates, not an envelope change. It was NOT shipped here because an acceptance batch is test-only by construction and user-facing copy is a product call (the ADIM 65 precedent on capability `dependency` text). It was NOT moved to class D either: B -> D would RAISE the D ceiling, and ceilings only fall except by adjudication.
